chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh and Sindiyy ibn Muhammad from Safwan ibn Yahya from Shu'ayb al-Aqarquti who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman who had a husband, and he did not know. He said: The woman is stoned, and there is no penalty upon the man if he did not know. I mentioned that to Abu Basir, who said to me: By God, Jafar (peace be upon him) said: The woman is stoned and the man is lashed with the legal punishment, and he said with his hands on his chest scratching it: I do not think that our Master's knowledge was complete. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: There is no contradiction between what Shu'ayb narrated from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and what Abu Basir heard from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), because what Abu Basir heard was regarding the case where the man married her while he knew that she had a husband, and the penalty was incumbent upon him as well because he was an adulterer. There is no contradiction between the two reports and the two legal opinions; rather, the matter became confused for Abu Basir, so he did not distinguish one question from the other, and he assumed that there was a contradiction between them.

key_terms.يُجلَدُ الحَدّ: He is lashed with the legal punishment (flogging)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in punishment for a man who marries a married woman if he didn't know versus if he did know?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Ishtibār elucidates the principle of *khata’* (mistake) in marital contracts, distinguishing between a man who marries a *muhsanah* in ignorance versus one who knows her status. Shaykh al-Tusi’s compiler, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, resolves the apparent contradiction between Imam al-Sadiq’s and Imam al-Rida’s rulings by clarifying that the former applies to the ignorant party while the latter applies to the knowing party, thereby affirming the consistency of the Imams' jurisprudence.
